overview: Canadian Pacific Kansas City Limited (CPKC) owns and operates the only single-line transcontinental freight railway connecting Canada, the United States, and Mexico, formed by the April 2023 merger of Canadian Pacific Railway and Kansas City Southern. The ~20,000-mile network hauls bulk commodities (grain, coal, potash, fertilizer, sulphur), merchandise freight (energy, chemicals/plastics, metals, forest products, automotive) and intermodal containers for industrial, agricultural, and consumer-goods shippers. Headquartered in Calgary, CPKC is a Class I railroad reporting US-GAAP-reconciled financials via 40-F and is listed on both the NYSE and TSX.

business_model.summary: CPKC earns freight revenue by moving carload and intermodal volumes across three traffic groups — bulk, merchandise, and intermodal — priced on a combination of fuel-surcharge-adjusted contract and spot rates per revenue ton-mile/carload. Revenue is largely volume- and price- (yield-) driven rather than subscription-like, but is relatively stable and repeat-business in nature given multi-year shipper contracts, high switching costs, and inelastic demand for rail-dependent bulk commodities.

revenue_streams.name: Other merchandise (forest products, metals, minerals, potash/fertilizer, consumer products)

business_model.customer_type: B2B — large industrial, agricultural, energy, automotive, and intermodal/logistics shippers (grain co-ops, oil & gas producers, chemical manufacturers, automakers, ocean carriers and 3PLs)
business_model.geographic_mix: Canada (Western grain belt, Vancouver/Montreal ports), US Midwest/Gulf Coast (ex-KCS network), and Mexico (Mexico City, Monterrey, industrial corridor) — single-line service across all three countries; post-merger ~45% Canada / ~40% US / ~15% Mexico-linked traffic approximate split

competitive_position.market_position: One of seven North American Class I railroads; the only railroad offering single-line service from Canada through the US heartland into Mexico. Roughly comparable scale to CN in Canada; smaller than Union Pacific or BNSF in the US but uniquely positioned on Mexico cross-border corridors alongside BNSF and UP (which interchange rather than own single-line Mexico routes).

moat_factors.description: Only Class I able to move freight across all three NAFTA/USMCA countries without an interchange handoff, reducing transit time, cost, and loss/damage versus interline competitors — difficult to replicate given rail rights-of-way scarcity and regulatory barriers to new rail construction.
Building a competing transcontinental rail network is practically impossible; existing rights-of-way, STB/CTA economic regulation, and capital intensity (tens of billions) protect incumbents.

Shippers with rail-served facilities (grain elevators, refineries, auto plants) face high costs to re-route to trucking or competing rail, especially where CPKC has the only line serving a given origin/destination.
Combined network supports density-driven cost efficiencies and cross-selling of new single-line intermodal/grain/automotive lanes (merger revenue synergies).
Operates in a rail industry structurally organized as regional duopolies (UP/BNSF in the West, CSX/NS in the East, CN/CPKC in Canada), limiting direct head-to-head rate competition on many lanes.

weaknesses: Smaller absolute scale than Union Pacific and BNSF in the core US market, limiting negotiating leverage on some interline traffic
Operating ratio (~61-65%) still trails best-in-class Union Pacific (~59%), implying efficiency catch-up still underway post-merger
Heavy reliance on grain and energy/bulk commodities that are weather- and commodity-price-cyclical

Exposure to a pending Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern transcontinental merger, which — if approved — would create a larger single-line coast-to-coast competitor and could pressure CPKC's relative network-reach advantage and intermodal pricing

growth_drivers: KCS merger revenue synergies — management guiding to $1.4-1.5 billion in annualized synergy revenue by year-end 2026, concentrated in intermodal, grain, automotive, and cross-border chemicals

Mexico nearshoring — manufacturing relocation to Mexico (autos, industrials, electronics) driving freight growth; CPKC citing ~25% YoY growth in Mexico-linked rail tonnage and targeting ~$600 million in "land bridge" (Mexico-US-Canada intermodal corridor) revenue by year-end 2026
Record grain volumes/pricing — Q2 2026 grain revenue up 24% YoY on record Canadian and US crop movement, with demand expected to remain strong through Q3 2026
Intermodal growth — international intermodal expected to return to growth in H2 2026 as retailers and 3PLs shift volume from truck to rail across the combined network's new single-line lanes
Automotive segment recovery — record automotive volumes benefiting from Mexico-based vehicle production supply chains
Operating leverage/margin improvement — continued cost synergy capture and network fluidity improvements targeting a sub-60% operating ratio
Capital discipline — 2026 capex guided at ~C$2.65 billion (~15% below prior year), supporting improved free cash flow conversion, buybacks, and dividend growth

business.description: Grain, coal, and energy/chemicals together are a large share of revenue and are exposed to crop yields, weather, and energy-sector capex cycles.
Coal revenue down ~18-29% YoY in recent quarters as thermal coal demand secularly declines, a persistent revenue headwind.

If approved by the STB, would create a larger single-line coast-to-coast competitor, potentially eroding some of CPKC's unique network-reach advantage and intensifying competition for single-line intermodal and merchandise traffic.

business.risk: Execution risk on remaining merger integration
business.description: Full synergy capture and operating ratio improvement versus best-in-class peers (Union Pacific ~59% OR vs CPKC ~61-65%) still in progress three-plus years post-merger.

financial.description: Total debt roughly $24-25 billion post-merger (net debt/EBITDA ~3.0x per latest screen data); plans for continued debt issuance (C$1.8B notes in Oct 2026) to refinance/extend maturities.
Revenue and costs span three currencies; reported USD results (40-F US-GAAP reconciliation) are sensitive to CAD and MXN translation and FX volatility affecting yields.
Diesel fuel is a major variable cost; fuel surcharge mechanisms only partially and with a lag offset price swings.

regulatory.description: US rail rates, service obligations, and merger conditions (including conditions attached to the original CP-KCS approval) are subject to ongoing STB oversight; potential new rate-reregulation proposals are a recurring industry risk.

CPKC has had to temporarily hold back rail cars carrying fuel/petrochemicals from Texas into Mexico under new Mexican import-permit rules aimed at curbing fuel smuggling, disrupting cross-border energy-product traffic.

The formal USMCA joint review (launched 2026) could reset rules of origin and tighten China-content limits, directly affecting the Mexico nearshoring and cross-border automotive/intermodal volumes CPKC is counting on for growth; Section 301/tariff actions on non-USMCA-qualifying goods add further uncertainty even though USMCA-compliant goods remain largely exempt.
Increased US/Canada/Mexico rail safety rulemaking (following high-profile derailments in the industry) could raise compliance costs or constrain operations.

macro.description: Section 301 tariffs and reciprocal trade measures affecting Mexico, Canada, and China-linked goods could reduce cross-border volumes that are central to CPKC's growth thesis, even though rail/USMCA-qualifying goods are currently largely exempt.

macro.risk: Mexican cartel-linked fuel theft and security
macro.description: Widespread fuel theft/smuggling in Mexico (estimated 16-27% of national fuel consumption) has prompted new import permitting regimes that disrupt CPKC's cross-border fuel and petrochemical traffic, and broader security risk affects Mexican rail operations generally.
Rail volumes correlate with North American industrial production, auto sales, housing/construction, and global trade; a recession would pressure merchandise and intermodal volumes.
Droughts, floods, or extreme winter weather affect grain harvests, network velocity, and operating costs.

execution.description: CPKC negotiates with multiple unions (Teamsters Canada Rail Conference, Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen, etc.) across Canada, the US, and Mexico; the 2024 Canada rail labor dispute required government intervention/arbitration, and a new 5-year BLET tentative deal was reached October 2026 — recurring negotiation risk given multi-year contract cycles.
CEO Keith Creel has led the company through the KCS acquisition and integration; succession risk if leadership changes during continued integration.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: North American Class I rail industry is mature and consolidated (effectively two US regional duopolies plus two Canadian majors), with low-single-digit volume growth historically but with CPKC specifically guided to mid-single-digit RTM growth in 2026 driven by merger synergies and Mexico nearshoring; a pending Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern transcontinental merger, if approved, would reshape competitive dynamics industry-wide.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — freight rail volumes track industrial production, agricultural output, energy markets, and global trade flows; bulk commodities (grain) are also weather-dependent
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — capital-intensive business with meaningful debt load (net debt/EBITDA ~3.0x); higher rates raise refinancing costs (e.g., Oct 2026 C$1.8B note issuance) and pressure equity valuation multiples
macro_factors.currency_exposure: High — operates and reports across CAD, USD, and MXN; USMCA-area trade policy and FX translation materially affect reported results

recent_developments.event: CPKC reached a tentative five-year collective bargaining agreement with the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen covering ~250 employees; stock slipped to a three-month low despite the positive labor news, and the company confirmed Q3 2026 earnings for October 28, 2026 plus a planned C$1.8 billion Canadian note issuance to refinance debt.
CPKC set new September and quarterly grain volume records in both Canada and the US.

CPKC Q2 2026 earnings call and investor commentary reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for mid-single-digit revenue ton-mile growth and double-digit (low-double-digit) earnings growth, citing synergy revenue on track for $1.4-1.5 billion by year-end and land-bridge (Mexico-US-Canada) revenue targeted at $600 million by year-end.

Q2 2026 results: revenue of $4.2 billion (+13% YoY), reported diluted EPS of $1.15 (down 14% YoY on prior-year one-time items), core adjusted diluted EPS of $1.27 (+13% YoY); record grain (+24% revenue/+19% volume), automotive (+22%), and energy/chemicals (+9%) revenue, partially offset by an 18-29% decline in coal; reported operating ratio 64.6% (core adjusted 61.6%).

CPKC temporarily held back rail cars carrying fuel and petrochemical shipments from Texas (Brownsville/Laredo) into Mexico after new Mexican import-permit regulations targeting fuel smuggling, pending shippers' permit documentation.

Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern advanced their proposed transcontinental merger through the STB review process; if approved, it would create a new US coast-to-coast single-line railroad and reshape competitive dynamics for all Class I carriers including CPKC.

CPKC and the Teamsters Canada Rail Conference concluded a new collective agreement (effective Jan 2024-Dec 2027, ~3% annual wage increases) covering locomotive engineers, conductors, and traffic controllers, following the 2024 Canada rail labor dispute that required federal arbitration intervention.

items.notes: RTMs reported up ~4% year-to-date through Q2 and nearly 7% quarter-to-date entering H2 2026.
Management reaffirmed another year of double-digit earnings growth, citing accelerating volumes and yields in H2 2026.
Driven by US-Mexico trade, cross-border intermodal, grain, automotive and cold-storage services; concentrated in intermodal and grain.
Specific sub-component of synergy revenue tied to the unique three-country single-line network.
Management frames lower capex as improving free-cash-flow conversion while supporting buybacks and the dividend, following a prior ~15% reduction to FY2025 capex guidance as well.
Management continues to target further operating ratio improvement toward Union Pacific's best-in-class ~59% level; Q2 2026 core adjusted OR was 61.6%.

items.target: sequential improvement in cents-per-RTM; coal remains a headwind but improving gradually; international intermodal returns to growth; grain demand strong through Q3 with normal-crop assumption for Q4
items.notes: Less casualty expense expected in H2 2026 versus H1.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Keith Creel stated CPKC is "well-positioned to accelerate volume and earnings growth in the second half of 2026," emphasizing continued synergy realization and disciplined cost control. Management highlighted strength in grain, energy/chemicals, and automotive, with coal remaining a structural headwind, and reiterated confidence in a path to $1.4-1.5 billion in synergy revenue and improving free cash flow conversion from lower planned capex.

bull_case: Only Class I railroad offering single-line Canada-US-Mexico service — a structurally difficult-to-replicate network moat that directly benefits from the Mexico nearshoring trend
Merger synergies still ramping toward a $1.4-1.5 billion annualized revenue run-rate by year-end 2026, providing a multi-year earnings growth tailwind independent of the broader freight cycle

Record performance in grain, automotive, and energy/chemicals segments in 2026, with management guiding to double-digit adjusted EPS growth and continued operating ratio improvement toward best-in-class peer levels
Disciplined, declining capital expenditure plan (down ~15% YoY to ~C$2.65B) supports improving free cash flow conversion, buybacks, and dividend growth as the KCS integration matures
Rail's structural cost/environmental advantage over long-haul trucking, plus congestion at US-Mexico border crossings, is pushing incremental freight onto CPKC's single-line network
bear_case: A combined Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern transcontinental railroad, if approved by the STB, would create a larger single-line US coast-to-coast competitor, diluting some of CPKC's unique cross-border network advantage and intensifying competition for intermodal and merchandise traffic

Coal revenue is in structural decline and Mexico cross-border fuel/petrochemical shipments face new regulatory friction (Mexican import permitting aimed at fuel-theft/smuggling), creating near-term revenue and operational disruption

USMCA review and ongoing tariff/trade-policy uncertainty directly threaten the Mexico nearshoring and cross-border automotive/intermodal growth thesis that underpins much of management's synergy and land-bridge revenue targets

Elevated leverage (~3x net debt/EBITDA) from the KCS acquisition combined with continued debt issuance (C$1.8B notes in Oct 2026) leaves the balance sheet more exposed to refinancing and interest-rate risk than before the merger

Operating ratio still trails Union Pacific's best-in-class level more than three years post-merger, and labor negotiations across three countries (Teamsters, BLET, Mexican unions) remain a recurring source of disruption risk, as seen in the 2024 Canada rail labor dispute
